title: Mara and the Rivergate
premise: When a government survey team vanishes near the Rivergate, a sealed canyon at the head of the Kestrel River, disgraced mountain guide Lena Nakamura is the only person both desperate enough and skilled enough to be hired for the search. Following the river upstream, she discovers the team was hunting a hidden valley that holds proof her late father, a cartographer branded a fraud, had mapped it truthfully decades ago. Betrayed by her employer, who wants the valley erased to protect a dam contract, Lena must choose between exposing the truth that would restore her name and protecting the isolated community living in the valley. In the end she floods the survey records into the river itself, letting the water carry the evidence downstream, and walks out of the canyon cleared of blame but changed by what inheritance really means.
about_author: Casper Marchetti is the pen name of a former river ranger who spent six seasons patrolling remote headwaters before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about landscapes that keep secrets and the people stubborn enough to go looking.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Working a low-paying trail crew job in a border town, Lena reflects on seven years of exile since the incident that got her blacklisted, measuring life in miles walked rather than years lived. When a government liaison finds her and offers a search contract for the vanished survey team, pride and need collide. Emotional beat: restless resignation cracking open into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the last known campsite of the survey team, she finds equipment neatly stacked, food untouched, and not a single footprint leaving the site — impossible even for her. The liaison, a smooth official named Aldous Vane, downplays the anomaly. Emotional beat: professional unease deepening into dread; something here doesn't obey the rules of mountains.

chapters.title: Terms of the Contract
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vane offers triple pay but demands absolute secrecy and a clause giving the ministry ownership of anything she finds. Lena signs anyway, telling herself it's just money for a fresh start abroad. A brief flashback shows her father teaching her to read contour lines as a child. Emotional beat: self-deception; she knows she's selling something she can't name.

chapters.title: Downstream People
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the river town of Ferrow's Landing, locals refuse to guide her past the gorge, muttering that the Rivergate 'keeps its own.' An old ferrywoman, Sela, warns her cryptically: 'Your father asked the same question.' Lena realizes her family name means something here. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that her exile is only about her own mistake.

chapters.title: Into the Gorge
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She enters the Rivergate alone, a slot canyon where the river narrows and the light dies. Navigation is brutal; she loses radio contact on day one. She finds a survey marker defaced with a symbol matching one from her father's old notebooks. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into focus — this is no longer a search, it's a pilgrimage.

chapters.title: The First Survivor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Ryn Okafor, junior member of the missing survey team, hiding in a cave above the waterline. Ryn watched the team leader destroy their own maps and walk into the river deliberately. Now starving, Ryn hears someone climbing below. Emotional beat: terror warring with the desperate hope of being found.

chapters.title: Unlikely Company
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lena and Ryn find each other; trust is slow, since Ryn assumes Lena is ministry muscle sent to silence witnesses. Ryn reveals the team found a warm-water channel leading behind the canyon wall — and that Vane ordered all findings buried. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming out of mutual necessity and shared suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Water Hides
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Following the warm channel, they discover a natural passage behind a waterfall. Ryn recounts the team leader's final words: 'Some maps are confessions.' Lena recognizes the phrase — it's her father's, verbatim. Emotional beat: grief surfacing; her father's disgrace may have been an erasure, not an error.

chapters.title: The Valley Behind the Wall
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They emerge into a hidden alpine valley, ice-free in winter, fed by geothermal springs — the true source of the Kestrel. A small community lives there, descendants of families who fled persecution generations ago. They are greeted not with welcome but with drawn bows. Emotional beat: awe colliding with hostility; paradise with a gatekeeper.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Community elder Ivo Marsh's POV. Ivo interrogates Lena and reveals her father reached the valley thirty years ago, promised to keep it secret, then published partial maps under pressure — which is why he was destroyed as a fraud and why the valley trusts no outsiders. Lena is judged by a debt she never knew existed. Emotional beat: shame inherited like an heirloom.

chapters.title: Seven Years Measured in Miles
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Confined to the valley while the elders deliberate, Lena confronts the truth of her own blacklist: her 'mistake' seven years ago was reporting unsafe conditions on a commercial expedition, and powerful people buried her to protect themselves. Her father's fate and hers are the same story twice told. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into clarity about who writes the records.

chapters.title: Vane Ascending
chapters.summary: Aldous Vane's POV. Back in the lowlands, Vane spins the team's disappearance to the press and mobilizes a 'rescue' force that is actually a survey-and-seal operation: dam the upper gorge, drown the passage, erase the valley forever. He names Lena publicly as a suspect. Emotional beat: cold bureaucratic menace; the antagonist believes he is the reasonable one.

chapters.title: The Choice Offered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The elders offer Lena a bargain: stay in the valley forever, safe and anonymous, and they will help clear her name quietly — or leave and be treated as an enemy. Ryn urges accepting; the valley has kept them alive. Lena sees the offer for what it is: another kind of blacklist, gilded. Emotional beat: temptation weighed against integrity.

chapters.title: Her Father's Last Map
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Given access to her father's confiscated field notes, Lena finds his final map — not of terrain, but of the water system itself, annotated with a warning: the gorge cannot be dammed without catastrophic flooding downstream, including Ferrow's Landing. Vane's project would kill hundreds. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — her legacy is not shame but a warning she must deliver.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Ryn, terrified of the coming confrontation, steals part of the map archive intending to trade it to Vane for amnesty. Caught by valley watchers, Ryn faces exile into the gorge alone. Lena intervenes, arguing mercy — because she knows what exile costs. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by fear; forgiveness extended at personal risk.

chapters.title: The Descent Race
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Learning Vane's crews have already entered the gorge with demolition equipment, Lena leads a small party — Ryn, Ivo's daughter Tamsin, and two valley scouts — downriver through the night to reach the dam site first. The descent nearly kills them at a cataract. Emotional beat: urgency and sacrifice; every mile bought with pain.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Witnesses
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the dam worksite, they disable the drilling rig and confront the crew chief, who doesn't know what his orders truly mean. Lena broadcasts her father's flood-warning data to the workers' radios. Some crews stand down; others radio Vane. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon that cuts both ways — exposure brings rescue and danger together.

chapters.title: Vane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Cornered by leaked data and mutinous crews, Vane attempts to trigger the diversion charges early, gambling that a controlled flood will bury the evidence and the witnesses. Lena reaches the charge station as the countdown runs. Emotional beat: the antagonist's logic collapsing into desperation; the climax ignites.

chapters.title: The River Decides
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax. In a brutal fight at the charge station, Lena cannot disarm the main charge — so she reroutes the detonation into the abandoned survey tunnel, collapsing the passage harmlessly inward instead of flooding the valley or the lowlands. Vane is swept into the gorge he meant to weaponize. Emotional beat: triumph earned through improvisation and nerve, not firepower.

chapters.title: After the Flood That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs briefly. The ministry, facing public outrage over Vane's scheme and Lena's broadcast evidence, formally clears her record and posthumously restores her father's reputation. The valley's existence remains officially unconfirmed — a secret now guarded by choice rather than force. Emotional beat: vindication arriving quieter than expected, and meaning less than hoped.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The elders invite Lena to stay — genuinely this time. She declines, but accepts a new role: annual cartographic envoy, the same work her father began, done honestly. She gives Ryn her spare gear and a recommendation that opens doors the blacklist once closed. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the past; identity rebuilt on chosen terms.

chapters.title: Miles Ahead
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, closing frame mirroring chapter one. Standing at the mouth of the Rivergate at dawn, Lena measures her life again in miles — but now the miles point somewhere. She shoulders her pack and starts downstream toward Ferrow's Landing, where Sela waits with the ferry. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; the journey ends where belonging begins.
